case: Backpack removal with required scenery and motion preservation
integration_context: This failure remains a rejection of the proposed general preservation fix. Exposing video input with documented limitations does not reclassify this output or establish reliable source-scene preservation.
prompt: Edit Video 1 into a continuous five-second photorealistic shot. Remove the black backpack and its straps from the hiker entirely. Keep the same man, face, dark trousers, shirt, hat, walking path and pose. Preserve the rocky mountain landscape, lighting, perspective and moving camera. Follow the source action for the first 3.042 seconds, then continue the same shot naturally until five seconds. No cuts, titles, subtitles, new objects, or duplicate subjects. Appropriate natural ambience; no dialogue or music.

reference.preparation: ffmpeg -v error -i hike_raw_24fps.mp4 -map 0:v:0 -an -frames:v 73 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -pix_fmt yuv420p hiker-reference.mp4
reference.preparation_rechecked: Reproduced byte-identical reference file during this integration.

scope.method: Labelled, nonblind sequential image review. All 120 candidate and 73 source frames reviewed in contact sheets; native candidate frames 0,36,72,119 and source frames 0,36,72 checked. Actual encoded comparison frames 0,36,72,119 checked.
scope.playback: No real-time playback by the agent.
scope.audio: Media and nonsilence validation only; no listening or human acceptance of this H1 output.
scope.limits: Fine facial identity, occluded anatomy, precise biomechanical naturalness and perceptual audio quality are not certified.

obligations.name: Backpack and straps removed from the beginning without remnants.
obligations.observation: No visible backpack or backpack straps in candidate frames 0..119, including the opening. Occluded body regions are not certified.

obligations.name: Person identity, clothes other than the removed backpack, movement and mountain setting preserved.
obligations.observation: Clothing categories and one foreground male hiker broadly persist, but the rocky setting, camera perspective/framing and same-time body pose/path change from frame 0. Exact facial identity is not qualified.

keyframes.observation: Source has a close rock wall and large bright boulders on the left; candidate replaces the near-left rocks and already shows broad blue sky and a distant pointed mountain composition. Human framing and stride differ.
Source keeps the close slope/left boulders and the hiker looking ahead/right; candidate shows an open valley/treeline and a downward-facing hiker with a different stride.
Source remains on the original rocky slope with the hiker turned farther away; candidate has a different green valley and mountain composition, posture and camera view.

obligations.name: One hiker, coherent shoulders and arms.
obligations.observation: One foreground hiker throughout and broadly coherent shoulders/arms in inspected frames. No clear duplicate foreground hiker, cut or title was found. Detailed gait/anatomy and real-time naturalness are not certified.

conclusion: The fixed high-canvas Ref4 Dense candidate removes the backpack but fails source-scene, camera and motion preservation on the first independent holdout. It does not meet all editing obligations and must not be adopted into stable.
boundaries: Failure is already visible at frame 0 inside the source-supported interval; continuation after 3.042 seconds cannot alone explain it.
No low-canvas H1 result exists. This does not establish that the high canvas caused or worsened preservation drift.
This run is true Dense. VSA is not necessary for this observed failure, but no unique root module or complete Turbo/native-model attribution is established.
